facts.fact_text: On 24 November 2006, the applicant announced to the Budapest Police Department his intention to organise a demonstration on 9 December 2006 on Kossuth Square in Budapest, in front of Parliament.
The announcement of 24 November 2006 was made as required by the Assembly Act 1989.
On 26 November 2006, the Budapest Police Department refused to deal with the applicant's application to organise a demonstration on Kossuth Square.
On 23 October 2006, the Budapest Police Department declared the area of Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone' (biztonsági műveleti terület) for an indefinite period of time.

The Budapest Police Department observed that the designation of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone' placed it outside the Budapest Police Department's jurisdiction as regards the prohibition of, or acquiescence in, a demonstration.

On 11 November 2010, the Budapest Regional Court issued judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9., quashing both the first-instance and the second-instance administrative decisions concerning the declaration of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone'.

The Budapest Regional Court in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. pointed out that the impugned administrative decisions did not contain any concrete elements establishing the necessity and proportionality of maintaining the 'security operational zone' after the prolongation of 22 November 2006.

The Budapest Regional Court in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. pointed out that the impugned administrative decisions did not address Mr K.'s suggestion that the mere fencing-off of Parliament's immediate vicinity, rather than the global ban on Kossuth Square, would have been sufficient in the circumstances.

On 4 April 2011, the Budapest Police Commander noted that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, the proportionality of the 'security operational zone' measure had successfully been challenged by Mr K.
